note.text:
Two figures are congruent if they have exactly the same shape and the same size: one fits exactly on top of the other.
• Corresponding sides are equal and corresponding angles are equal.
• We write ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR. The order of the letters shows which vertices correspond: A ↔ P, B ↔ Q, C ↔ R, so AB = PQ, BC = QR, CA = RP.
• Translations, rotations and reflections give congruent images; an enlargement (scale factor not 1) does not.
• Similar figures have the same shape but may differ in size.

sections.heading: Same shape, same size
sections.text:
Two figures are congruent if one can be placed exactly on top of the other. Their corresponding sides are equal and their corresponding angles are equal.
Two {500} FCFA coins are congruent. A large and a small photo of the same picture are not: they have the same shape but different sizes. Those are similar.

sections.heading: Naming the matching parts
sections.text:
When we write ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR, the order of the letters tells us which vertices match: A ↔ P, B ↔ Q, C ↔ R.
So AB = PQ, BC = QR and CA = RP, and angle A = angle P, angle B = angle Q, angle C = angle R.
Always match the letters in order; do not just look at the picture.

sections.heading: Moving without changing
sections.text:
Translation (sliding), rotation (turning) and reflection (flipping) move a figure without changing its lengths or angles, so the image is congruent to the object.
An enlargement with a scale factor other than {1} changes the size: the image is similar, not congruent.

key_words.meaning: same shape, possibly a different size

examples: ΔABC ≅ ΔDEF: AB = DE, angle C = angle F
A reflected triangle is congruent to the original.

mistake.why: Match the letters in order: B ↔ Q and C ↔ R.

worked_example.problem: ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR. AB = {p} cm, BC = {q} cm, CA = {r} cm, angle A = {x}° and angle B = {y}°. Find QR and angle R.
steps: The letters match in order: A ↔ P, B ↔ Q, C ↔ R.
QR corresponds to BC, so QR = {q} cm.
Angle R corresponds to angle C = {180} − {x} − {y} = {180 - x - y}°.
worked_example.answer: QR = {q} cm, angle R = {180 - x - y}°

cards.idea: Congruent figures have the same shape and the same size.
example: Two copies of the same exercise book cover are congruent.

cards.idea: In ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR the letters match in order: AB = PQ, BC = QR, CA = RP.
Translations, rotations and reflections keep the size: the image is congruent.
example: An enlargement changes the size: the image is only similar.

pick.q: Which transformation always gives an image congruent to the object?
w: An enlargement with scale factor ½
e: Scale factor 2 doubles the lengths: similar, not congruent.
Scale factor ½ halves the lengths.
A stretch changes the shape.

pick.q: A triangle is reflected in a line. The image is…
e: A reflection keeps every length.
A reflection keeps the size.
A reflection keeps the shape.
pick.y: Reflections keep lengths and angles: the image is congruent.

pick.q: Which of these does NOT give a congruent image?
e: A translation slides the shape without changing it.
A rotation turns the shape without changing it.
A reflection flips the shape without changing its size.

pick.q: What does it mean for two figures to be congruent?
w: Same shape, possibly a different size
e: That describes similar figures.
Different shapes can have the same area.
Different shapes can have the same perimeter.
pick.y: Congruent figures fit exactly on top of each other.

pick.q: Two triangles have the same angles but one is twice as big. They are…
e: Congruent figures must also be the same size.
Equal angles make them similar.
Different sizes: not congruent.

pick.r: Two squares with sides of 5 cm
w: Two rectangles with the same area
Two triangles with the same angles
e: Squares of different sizes are only similar.
A 2 × 8 and a 4 × 4 rectangle have the same area but different shapes.
Equal angles give similar triangles; they can differ in size.
pick.y: Same shape and the same side length: congruent.

questions.prompt: ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR. AB = {p} cm, BC = {q} cm and CA = {r} cm. Find {X.n}.

misconceptions.explain: Match the letters in order: {X.n} goes with {X.m}.

solution: The letters match in order: A ↔ P, B ↔ Q, C ↔ R.
where: p + q > r && q + r > p && p + r > q

questions.prompt: ΔABC ≅ ΔDEF. Angle A = {x}° and angle B = {y}°. Find angle F.

misconceptions.explain: F matches C, not A: the third letters correspond.

pick.q: ΔKLM ≅ ΔXYZ. Which side equals LM?
e: XY matches KL.
XZ matches KM.
Sides are named within one triangle.
pick.y: L ↔ Y and M ↔ Z, so LM = YZ.

pick.q: ΔABC ≅ ΔRTS. Which angle equals angle C?
e: T matches B.
R matches A.
Every angle has a partner.
pick.y: The third letters correspond: C ↔ S.

pick.q: ΔPQR ≅ ΔMNO. Which side equals RP?
e: MN matches PQ.
NO matches QR.
Sides are named within one triangle.
pick.y: R ↔ O and P ↔ M, so RP = OM.
